Continuous-index adapted process is independently sourced, but only discrete-time filtration has a checked direct source in the corpus; do not link it to real-index adaptedness as if equivalent.
Chromatic polynomial equivalence is still research-only; MathWorld is not in vetted source registry. A new source registration, rights review and exact citation are required before ingesting it.
Metric/nonempty ProofWiki convention was preserved in Batch98; no empty metric-space convention admitted without an additional independent source.

The generic scalar division-ring normed-vector foundation was source- and meaning-screened in Batches100–102 with correct multiplicative and left/right scope; original standalone ProofWiki Normed Division Ring page lists no bibliographic citations. A separate external authority should corroborate when feasible.
Current scalar normed vector source is left-oriented; no right-normed-vector formulation should be automatically generated without specifically sourced right-action homogeneity axioms.

ProofWiki calls its selected-point global-domain bound 'Lipschitz at a point', which is NOT equivalent to neighborhood-local two-point Lipschitz continuity; preserve this distinction in later variant comparisons.
The two tree formulations, no circuits/no cycles, are equivalent only in the stated simple connected undirected graph context; no root or finite-cardinality convention inferred.
Independent sigma-algebra countable-family property imposes all finite distinct-index products; pairwise independence alone does not imply mutual independence for three or more.

ProofWiki Definition:Boundary (Topology) 'Definition from Closure and Exterior' appears false as written: it takes subset of A and omits closure boundary points outside A. Excluded from Batch106/107/108; separate source-audit should note this.

The general closure source also has closure=A union boundary; it was not ingested because allowing boundary to depend on closure and closure to depend on boundary would form a definition expansion cycle. Source-preserved noncircular closed-superset formulations were admitted instead.

Potential source issue for later independent investigation: ProofWiki's Definition:Directional Derivative gives ∇f·u assuming 'gradient exists', while partial derivatives may exist without total differentiability; do not treat as automatically equivalent to line-direction limit on that assumption.
ProofWiki source-specific finite-image rank requires the image of a field-vector-space linear transformation to be finite-dimensional; no automatic cardinal-valued or arbitrary-module rank extension.
Accumulation point of a sequence (infinitely many indices in each neighborhood) differs from accumulation point of its value SET (closure of A minus the tested point); do not collapse variants.
